title: Grace to a broken women part 1
scripture_text: ‘’Jesus went to the Mount of Olives. At dawn he appeared again in the temple courts, where all the people gathered around him, and he sat down to teach them. The teachers of the law and the Pharisees brought in a woman caught in adultery. They made her stand before the group and said to Jesus, “Teacher, this woman was caught in the act of adultery. In the Law, Moses commanded us to stone such women. Now what do you say?” They were using this question as a trap, in order to have a basis for accusing him. But Jesus bent down and started to write on the ground with his finger. When they kept on questioning him, he straightened up and said to them, “Let any one of you who is without sin be the first to throw a stone at her.” Again he stooped down and wrote on the ground. At this, those who heard began to go away one at a time, the older ones first, until only Jesus was left, with the woman still standing there. Jesus straightened up and asked her, “Woman, where are they? Has no one condemned you?” “No one, sir,” she said. “Then neither do I condemn you,” Jesus declared. “Go now and leave your life of sin.”
devotional:
People need grace.

It was the memorial service for Hubert Humphrey, long-time senator from Minnesota, and one-time nominee as Democratic candidate for US President. The church was packed with dignitaries, but one man stood alone, shunned by most of the congregation. Only a few years before, Richard M. Nixon had resigned the Presidency, and although he’d been given a pardon by Gerald Ford he was still regarded by many as a ‘crook’. It was Nixon’s first visit to Washington since that shameful day when he departed the White House in a Marine helicopter and it seemed that nobody at the church that day wanted to engage with him. However, when President Jimmy Carter entered the building greeting friends and colleagues, he noticed Nixon standing off in the distance. Walking over to him, Carter took Nixon’s hand and embraced him, saying for all to hear "Welcome Home, Mr. President."

That simple act, became the turning point for Mr. Nixon and led to a period of true forgiveness that allowed him to be regarded as one of the elder statesmen of the country until his death.

If we really understood how powerful and freeing grace was, we would pursue it with all our being. If we truly grasped the effects grace can have on hurting individuals and families, then we would eagerly want to show grace to all. People who are full of grace are the most God-like and are thus those who have real freedom, authority and influence.

Unfortunately we live in a world that is ungracious, a world where the strong dominate the weak, and the rich exploit the poor. We live in a world where mercy has become unfashionable, and grace has been reduced to a word more readily associated with ballet. As people, we have two basic needs when it comes to grace. We need to receive it and we need to show it!

No matter who we are, be we an American President, or a homeless beggar, rich or poor, known or unknown, successful or not, we all are in a desperate need to receive grace. However, we all have just a similar need to show grace to others. Showing grace to others is not just some saintly virtue reserved for those who are perceived to be ‘super spiritual.’ Rather showing grace to others is the truest expression of our humanity, a humanity that has been made in the image of God.

As we read this story of Jesus’ encounter with the woman who had been caught in adultery, we can see that it has a lot to teach us about the power of grace. It’s a story that says something about God’s response to sexual sin, but it’s only not about sexual sin. There’s a lesson here about how we should respond to others who sin sexually and about the danger of self-righteousness which is, by its very nature, is in contrast with grace.

In his book Mere Christianity, C. S. Lewis says,

‘’If anyone thinks that Christians regard un-chastity (sexual sin) as the supreme vice, he is quite wrong. The sins of the flesh are bad, but they are the least bad of all sins. All the worst pleasures are purely spiritual. The pleasure of putting other people in the wrong, of bossing and patronizing and spoiling sport, and backbiting; the pleasures of power, of hatred. For there are two things inside me...they are the animal self and the diabolical self; and the diabolical self is the worst of the two. That is why a cold self-righteous prig who goes regularly to church may be far nearer to hell than a prostitute. But of course it is better to be neither! reddit.com Accessed 12/04/2025

In the story recorded in John 7:53-8:10, Jesus confronts what C. S. Lewis would call a band of ‘cold, self-righteous prigs’ and a woman who was guilty of open sexual sin. He handles both with such wisdom and grace that the story has become a favourite of many.
prayer: Father help me to understand that I have been created to receive and share grace.
